exhibits.title: The Gathering of Sparks
exhibits.text: A swarm of golden sparks hangs above the basin in pure disorder — this is x_T, drawn straight from the Well of Chance as x_T ~ N(0,1), with T ≈ 1000. Nothing is written in that chaos; it is the same blank noise for every image the palace will ever conjure. Watch the swarm long enough and you will see GENERATION itself: breath by breath the sparks drift into rank until a figure — two crescent moons — stands where nothing was, the backward walk x_T → x_{T-1} → … → x₀ made visible. Then the figure is surrendered to chaos again, and the walk begins anew. Each backward step is a single ritual of three movements. FIRST, ask the trained network what noise it sees: ε_pred = net(x_t, t). SECOND, perform THE REARRANGEMENT — solve the forward equation x_t = √ᾱₜ·x₀ + √(1−ᾱₜ)·ε for the clean image, giving an estimate x₀_est = (x_t − √(1−ᾱₜ)·ε_pred) / √ᾱₜ. THIRD, do NOT trust that estimate all the way home; use it to compute only the next rung down, x_{t-1}. Watch one rung with real numbers. At t=3 the swarm reads x₃=4.478 and the net predicts ε_pred=0.38. With √(1−ᾱ₃)=0.521 and √ᾱ₃=0.854 the rearrangement gives x₀_est = (4.478 − 0.521·0.38) / 0.854 = 4.280 / 0.854 = 5.012. The true clean value hidden in the noise was 5.0 — remarkably close from a single guess. Yet the walk does not leap to 5.012 and stop. It steps to x₂, looks again with fresh eyes, and asks again. Why the timid steps instead of the bold jump? Read the plaques. Why each step stirs a pinch of fresh chaos back in before it settles? Read on. The whole loop is nothing but: for t = T down to 1 — predict, rearrange, step — return x₀.

exhibits.title: Why Small Steps, Not One Bold Jump
exhibits.text: If x₀_est is so close at t=3, why not simply output it and be done? Because t=3 is near the END of the walk, where almost all noise is already gone and the guess is easy. Rewind to the start: at t=900 the candelabra is near-pure glare, and the network is asked to guess the finished image from what is essentially static. That estimate is ROUGH — a hunch, not a portrait. The x₀_est is only trustworthy as t → 0. So the ritual never commits the whole distance on one rough hunch. It takes the current best guess, steps back just ONE level of noise, then RE-ESTIMATES with fresh eyes at t-1 — where slightly less noise makes the next guess a little sharper. A thousand humble re-estimations, each correcting the last, arrive far truer than one confident leap from the fog.

exhibits.title: The Reverse Formula — Re-Noise, Then a Kick
exhibits.text: The DDPM step reads: x_{t-1} = √ᾱ_{t-1}·x₀_est + √(1−ᾱ_{t-1})·ε_pred + σₜ·z. Read it as a sentence. Take your BEST GUESS of the clean image (√ᾱ_{t-1}·x₀_est), then RE-NOISE it — but only back to level t-1, not the level t you came from — by adding √(1−ᾱ_{t-1})·ε_pred, and finally deliver a small RANDOM KICK σₜ·z with z ~ N(0,1). Follow the same candle from t=3 to t=2, using x₀_est=5.01, ε_pred=0.38, and ᾱ₂=0.81 so √ᾱ₂=0.9 and √(1−ᾱ₂)=0.436: x₂ = 0.9·5.01 + 0.436·0.38 = 4.509 + 0.166 = 4.675 (before the tiny kick). The candelabra drifted from x₃=4.478 to x₂=4.675 — leaning toward the clean value 5.0. It did not arrive; it merely walked one confident step closer, and will ask again.

exhibits.title: Why Re-Noise, and Why the Random Kick
exhibits.text: Re-noising sounds mad — why add noise back while trying to REMOVE it? Because you remove more than you add. Stepping t → t-1, the signal coefficient √ᾱ GROWS (0.854 → 0.9) while the noise coefficient √(1−ᾱ) SHRINKS (0.521 → 0.436): net noise falls with every rung, so the candelabra dims overall even as each step re-lights a little. Now the random kick σₜ·z, drawn — like every ε and every z in this palace — from the basement Well of Chance, N(0,1). Drop it and generation becomes DETERMINISTIC: every walk from the same fog lands on the same over-smoothed answer, the blurry AVERAGE of all plausible images. The kick keeps each descent slightly different, so samples come out SHARP and DIVERSE. It is added at every rung but ONE: at the final step to t=0 the kick is dropped, so the last breath lands on a clean, settled x₀ with no leftover jitter.

exhibits.title: One Rung of the Backward Walk
exhibits.spec:
graph TD
  X[x_t] --> N[ε_pred = net x_t, t]
  N --> R[rearrange:\nx0_est = x_t − √1−ᾱ·ε_pred / √ᾱ]
  R --> G[best guess:\n√ᾱ_t-1 · x0_est]
  N --> RN[re-noise to t-1:\n√1−ᾱ_t-1 · ε_pred]
  W[Well of Chance\nz ~ N 0,1] --> K[random kick:\nσ_t · z]
  G --> S[x_t-1]
  RN --> S
  K --> S
  S --> L[loop until x0]
exhibits.caption: Predict, rearrange, step. The best guess is re-noised only to level t-1 and given a small kick from the Well of Chance; the kick is dropped at the final step to x₀.

exhibits.title: From Pure Noise, an Image Precipitates — the Reverse Walk in Snapshots
exhibits.caption: The whole descent in five breaths. The leftmost cloud is x_T, pure N(0,1) — the same blank glare for every image the palace will ever conjure. Generation walks rightward, each snapshot one stretch of the reverse walk, as structure precipitates out of the static until two moons stand revealed at x₀. Every rung is the same ritual: predict the noise ε̂, rearrange to an estimate of x₀, step just one level down, and add a small fresh N(0,1) kick — dropped only at the final step so the last breath lands clean. Each point is coloured by its true home in the finished shape, so you can watch the moons gather even while they are still mostly noise.
